title: Make the Daisy
goal: Get a white edge on all four sides of the yellow center.
hold: Yellow center up, white center down

normalPath.heading: What to do
normalPath.instruction: Turn any side face until a white edge comes up next to the yellow center. Keep going until all four petals are white.

cases.when: A petal is flipped — the white sticker faces out instead of up.
cases.setup: Turn the top until the flipped petal is facing you.
cases.name: Daisy Edge Flipper

doneWhen: All four petals are white and facing up.

title: Make the White Cross
goal: Move the petals down to the bottom, with every color matching its center.
hold: Yellow center up, white center down

normalPath.heading: What to do
normalPath.instruction: Look at the side color of a petal. Turn the top until that color is facing you and matches the center in front of you. Then turn the whole front face twice to drop the petal to the bottom. Repeat for all four petals.
normalPath.note: The demo shows the last petal going in. Watch the cube tip over at the end to see the finished cross underneath.

doneWhen: There is a white cross on the bottom and every edge color matches the center above it.

title: Learn Your Two Triggers
goal: Memorize both of these. They are the most-used moves in the rest of the solve.
why: This is not a solving step — it is a tool you are picking up. Every cuber learns these first. The Left Trigger is not a second thing to memorize: it is the same move with your other hand.

algorithms.name: Right Trigger
algorithms.note: Also called the "sexy move" in the cubing world.

algorithms.name: Left Trigger
algorithms.note: The mirror of the Right Trigger.

doneWhen: You can do both without looking at the screen.

title: Finish the First Layer
goal: A solid white face on the bottom, with matching bands of color around the sides.
hold: White cross on the bottom, yellow up

normalPath.heading: What to do
normalPath.instruction: Find a white corner in the top layer. Turn the top until that corner sits directly above the slot it belongs in — the slot whose two colors match the corner's other two colors. Then repeat the Right Trigger until it drops into place.
normalPath.note: The demo shows one Right Trigger dropping the corner in. On your cube it may take more than one — keep repeating until it lands.

cases.when: A white corner is already in the bottom layer, but in the wrong slot or twisted the wrong way.
cases.setup: Hold that corner at the front-right, then run the Right Trigger once to pop it out into the top layer. Now solve it normally.
cases.name: Right Trigger (you already know this one)

doneWhen: The whole bottom face is white, and the side colors form solid matching bands.
